_comment: Route colour type guard (final review, IMPORTANT 1). GTFS route_color is
six hex digits with NO leading '#'; api.subwaynow.app currently adds one
itself, but nothing guarantees that stays true, and
render.Circle(color = '6cbe45') fails FATALLY if it isn't normalized first.
route_colors() must not trust the API's 'color' field shape at all.
Three malformed/edge shapes in one 'routes' payload:
G       -- bare six-hex-digit string (no '#'), the actual GTFS shape.
Must be normalized to '#6cbe45' and used to render, not
skipped -- north+south below exactly mirror the reference
fixture's own G35 trips (route G, FIX_N/G21, 30s -> 'now'),
so a correct normalization renders PIXEL-IDENTICAL to
reference/subway-64x32.png (checked via
'assert_matches_reference' below).
BADNUM  -- color is an int (123), not a string at all. Not used by
any trip here, but route_colors() iterates every routes
entry unconditionally on every render, so the type guard
must reject this without crashing regardless of whether
the route ever appears in a trip.
BADNAME -- color is a string but not a valid hex shape
('chartreuse', length 10). Same reasoning as BADNUM: must
be rejected without crashing, whether or not it's ever
assigned to a trip.
